criteria.name: Reproduction steps present
criteria.autoCheck: Look for numbered list or 'Steps to Reproduce' / 'Repro' section

criteria.name: Expected vs actual behavior documented
criteria.autoCheck: Look for 'Expected' and 'Actual' sections or descriptions

criteria.name: Acceptance criteria can close in phase
criteria.autoCheck: For each AC, ask which workflow phase owns its completion condition: implementation (resolves while the issue is worked), review (resolves after in_review), or release (resolves during /prepare-release). At the moment /work reaches Step 5 and gh pmu validates the checkboxes, is the condition knowably true? If not the AC is out of phase. This is NOT the same question as ac-testable / success-measurable, which ask whether a condition is well-defined — 'once released and re-imported, the config is revisited' is perfectly measurable and simply is not measurable YET. Re-read .claude/metadata/ac-feasibility-prompts.json from disk and apply phaseFeasibility.actionIfOutOfPhase: work listed in ownedElsewhere (CHANGELOG, tagging, release publication) should be DROPPED, not annotated, because another command's checklist already discharges it; a genuinely load-bearing gate should be ANNOTATED per annotationFormat with a gatePhases token. Report ❌ for an out-of-phase AC carrying no annotation, ⚠️ for one whose annotation is present but questionable. Also check each existing annotation in BOTH directions: a `→ GATE:` token whose AC text names no event that resolves it is reported (the token is being used to mean 'I cannot tick this now' rather than as a phase claim), and so is one whose named condition no gate phase describes or which is in fact satisfiable during implementation. An annotation is a claim about phase, not a licence to leave a box unchecked.

criteria.name: Environment info present
criteria.autoCheck: Look for 'Environment', browser, OS, version references

criteria.name: Severity proportionate to impact
criteria.autoCheck: Compare severity/priority label to described user impact (e.g., P0 for data loss, P2 for cosmetic)

criteria.name: Test coverage proportionate (bug)
criteria.autoCheck: Single-path fix: 'existing tests pass' may suffice, but regression test AC preferred. Multi-path refactor: ACs MUST require tests for new pattern (flag if only 'existing tests pass' for changes touching multiple functions/modules). Additionally report which test files the fix implicates, pairing inferred source paths against `.claude/skills/tdd-refactor-coverage-audit/resources/test-coverage-conventions.json` and naming each; where no pairing resolves, say that none could be resolved and why rather than reporting nothing. Advisory — blocks nothing.

criteria.name: Deployment impact assessed
criteria.autoCheck: Check for a 'Deployment Impact' section (or 'Impact: dev-only' / 'Impact: deployed') in the body. Validate the classification against framework-manifest.json deploymentFiles - the authority the issue corpus actually reasons from - together with the Stage 1 / Stage 2 command pipeline and deploy-dist.yml. Values: 'dev-only' = touches nothing that reaches a user project (framework scripts, Proposal/, PRD/, Archive/, tests, CHANGELOG); 'deployed' = touches a path carried by deploymentFiles or emitted by Stage 2, so it reaches user projects on hub update - list the affected areas; 'unknown' = the classification could not be determined and needs a human decision before the issue is worked.

criteria.name: Prior art checked
criteria.autoCheck: Delegate to decideSweep in .claude/scripts/shared/lib/prior-art-marker.js and report the status it returns; do not re-derive the rule here. The marker itself is the literal '**Prior Art:**' heading defined by .claude/metadata/prior-art-sweep.json bodyFormat.heading; present and complete = pass. Issues created before the cutoff in that helper are not applicable rather than failing. Behaviour past that depends on framework-config.json reviewSweep, a 4-mode setting since #2564 (absent = 'recommend'): under 'full' an absent or PARTIAL marker reports fail and runs the Step 2a-iv sweep; under 'recommend' it reports the advisory status 'recommend' and runs NO sweep — this must NOT be reported as fail, because --prior-art is opt-in and rarely passed, so most issues carry no marker and a fail would downgrade nearly every review; under 'flag-only' and 'off' report skip, not fail, which would downgrade every review in a project that opted out.
